findings.evidence: `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1034` (`calculateLeftOverlapPercent`) and `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1058` (`calculateRightOverlapPercent`) bound inputs via built-in `max`/`min` and then compute a ratio dividing by `histWidth^2` (e.g., `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1047`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1052`). In `OutOfRangeRowCount`, `histWidth := histR - histL` is only normalized for `< 0` and `+Inf` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1158`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1166`), so `histWidth` can be `NaN` (e.g., `Inf - Inf`), making `boundL/boundR` `NaN` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1167`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1168`) and causing the overlap helpers to return `NaN` due to `min/max` NaN propagation (confirmed via `go doc builtin min` / `go doc builtin max`: “if any args are NaNs, returns NaN”). Those percents flow into `totalPercent` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1184`) and then into `avgRowCount` / `finalEst` / `maxEst` (`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1187`, `pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1214`–`pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1222`). In the parent version (first parent), percent computation was guarded by overlap comparisons (e.g., `...^:pkg/statistics/histogram.go:1128`–`:1161`), so `NaN` bounds tended to short-circuit overlap and keep percents at 0, avoiding NaN propagation.
findings.fix: Treat NaN histogram widths/inputs as “invalid for overlap percent” to preserve finite estimates: (a) in `OutOfRangeRowCount`, add `if math.IsNaN(histWidth) { histWidth = 0 }` before computing `boundL/boundR`, and/or (b) in `calculateLeftOverlapPercent`/`calculateRightOverlapPercent`, early-return 0 when any of `l,r,bound*,hist*,histWidth` is NaN. Either approach restores the prior effective behavior (NaN bounds → 0% overlap) and prevents NaN poisoning.
findings.impact: If `histWidth` (or inputs) becomes NaN, `RowEstimate.Est/MaxEst` can become NaN and propagate into planner selectivity/costing. `RowEstimate.Clamp` and `mathutil.Clamp` do not sanitize NaN, so this can yield unstable plan choice behavior and potential downstream panics/undefined comparisons in code assuming finite row counts.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master` `pkg/statistics/histogram.go`: overlap helpers remain and there is still no `math.IsNaN(histWidth)` / input-NaN guard around overlap-percent computation.
findings.verify: Add a targeted unit test constructing a float histogram whose bounds are both `+Inf` (or both `-Inf`) and assert `OutOfRangeRowCount` returns finite (`!math.IsNaN`/`!math.IsInf`) `RowEstimate` fields for representative ranges. Optionally add a regression test with NaN predicate bounds (if ranger can produce them) to ensure the estimate remains finite.
findings.what: Potential NaN regression in out-of-range estimation: extracting overlap-percent math into helpers that use built-in `min/max` can propagate NaNs into `OutOfRangeRowCount` results when `histWidth` becomes NaN (e.g., `histL==histR==±Inf`) or range endpoints are NaN; the pre-refactor code largely avoided computing percents under NaN bounds via overlap-condition short-circuiting.

subject: statistics: refactor out of range percent calculations (#65857)
summary: Refactors `Histogram.OutOfRangeRowCount` overlap-percent computations into helper functions and updates planner cardinality suite expected output; introduces a plausible NaN-propagation edge case in out-of-range estimation when histogram width or inputs become NaN.
